corrected_verdict: KNOWN (upheld). The Alon-Roichman random Cayley graph argument, specialised to Z_p with a Hoeffding tail. McCracken et al. 2025 (Thm 4.7/Cor 4.8) is the direct modular-addition ML precedent. Only the budget normalisation into Gamma_s is ours.
issues: No missed prior art found beyond what the checker already has. McCracken et al. arXiv 2505.18266 Thm 4.7 is the direct ML precedent (random uniform frequencies from {1..n/2}, margin delta*m for all wrong k). Minor corrections: (a) The checker's transcription of Thm 4.7 is garbled. The actual condition is m > [2 ln n - 2 ln(2-2rho)] / [ln(pi/delta) - 1]. At delta=1/2 this needs m ~ 2.4 ln n versus our 8 ln p, so our constant is loose, which a reviewer may notice. (b) The existing mccracken2025 bib entry is wrong: the title is 'Uncovering a Universal Abstract Algorithm for Modular Addition in Neural Networks' and the authors are Gavin McCracken, Gabriela Moisescu-Pareja, Vincent Letourneau, Doina Precup, Jonathan Love (abs page fetched). (c) Alon-Roichman Thm 2 is confirmed from the PDF text: a multiset of (1+eps)log2 n elements chosen with repetition, a per-character bound, then a union over the n-1 nontrivial characters. Their per-character tail is binomial/Chernoff, not Hoeffding, so 'cyclic case of the argument' is fair. The bib is correct; add doi 10.1002/rsa.3240050203. (d) Naor-Naor and AGHP metadata are confirmed via Crossref, but both constructions are over Z_2^n and small-bias is two-sided (|E chi|<=eps). Calling our one-sided condition a '1/2-biased multiset of Z_p \citep{naor1993small}' stretches the definition. Keep it optional, phrased as 'a one-sided analogue of small-bias sets', or drop it. (e) The Hoeffding 1963 JASA 58(301):13-30 bib is confirmed via Crossref.
